INDEPENDENT CLOUD REVIEW of PR #32 at branch head 4305428f. Dispatched by
cron, not by the author; I did not see the author's session and read only this
branch plus the GitHub REST API. origin/main was FETCHED FRESH before any
state claim was evaluated (live main = bfe850796969980545811e1ffa551b9143965faf,
confirmed both by git fetch and by the REST commits/main endpoint).

VERDICT: DISAGREE. The SUBSTANCE of this correction is sound and I say so
before the findings: its central factual claim checks out against evidence I
could reach independently, its self-correction is real, and its own proof
record refuses to overclaim. I am disagreeing on four mechanical blockers,
every one of them a required check that is red or a merge that cannot happen.
None of them is an argument with the document.

=== WHAT I CONFIRMED IN THE DOCUMENT'S FAVOUR (measured, not assumed) ===
- PR #27 is merged (merged_at 2026-09-19T14:18:29Z, merge commit f9b4dea).
- reviews/27/cloud-reviewer.json ON MAIN does carry
  reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author: false, verdict AGREE, reviewer token
  01GaiKSWBCRLtcVa5fPYz4nQ. So the field this PR calls wrong is really there,
  really false, and really landed.
- The timeline corroborates a start near 13:59 rather than 13:23 or 14:23:
  reviewer A's comment on #27 is timestamped 14:09:46Z and the merge 14:18:29Z.
  A 14:23 cron start is after both. A 13:23 start would put roughly 47 minutes
  between dispatch and comment. Neither is impossible; the 13:59 account fits
  best. This is corroboration, NOT proof -- see the not-checked list.
- MUTATION PROBE of the document's corrected claim. The document says a record
  declaring reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author: true PASSES the gate with only
  a NOTICE. I built exactly such a record (AGREE, dispatched true, attesting
  the reviewable head) and ran
      python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base f9b4dea --head HEAD --pr-number 32
  Every "touches a shared path and has 0 independent review(s)" failure
  DISAPPEARED and was replaced by a NOTICE line saying the review is not
  independent by construction. So the dispatched-true record COUNTED as a
  satisfying independent review. The document's corrected statement is
  CORRECT, and the version it replaced was wrong, exactly as it says. The
  probe file was deleted immediately; the tree was clean before I committed.

=== F1 (NOT BLOCKING, but a real defect, and of the document's own class).
    The document makes a claim about ITSELF that is false at this head. ===
reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md says, of the record-only bypass it has just
described:
    "**This pull request is itself an instance.** A green `lwb-lanes` here is
     not evidence that anything in this file was reviewed."
Measured, it is not an instance any more. I classified every commit on the
branch with the gate's own predicate:
    RECORD-ONLY  4305428f  review(32) ...
    RECORD-ONLY  746d1226  review(32) ...
    RECORD-ONLY  1fa35df0  review(32) B ...
    reviewable   5e415c44  docs(handoff): regenerate LAST ...
    RECORD-ONLY  51fa05d4  docs(proof) ...
    RECORD-ONLY  3509d2fd  docs(reviews) ...
    RECORD-ONLY  2560e4b1  review(32) B ...
    RECORD-ONLY  7d089a8d  docs(reviews) ...
5e415c44 touches HANDOFF.md, which is neither under reviews/ nor under proof/,
so it is NOT record-only and resolve_reviewable_head returns it:
    lwb_lanes.resolve_reviewable_head('f9b4dea..HEAD') -> 5e415c44d50913...
A record must therefore attest 5e415c44, a commit OF THIS PULL REQUEST. And
    git diff 5e415c44 HEAD -- reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md
is EMPTY: the document at the attested head is byte-identical to the document
at the branch head. So a green lwb-lanes here WOULD be evidence that this file,
in its final form, was attested.
The sentence was TRUE when it was written, in 3509d2f, when every commit on
the branch really was under reviews/. Commit 5e415c44 added a HANDOFF.md write
one commit later and made it false. That is precisely the failure mode this
document exists to correct -- an exact claim about provenance that goes stale
under the next commit -- and this document has already had to correct itself
once for the same class. The underlying limitation it describes is real and I
am not disputing it; only the self-application is wrong. Suggested fix: keep
the limitation, replace the self-application with what is actually true here
(the branch stopped being an instance when the HANDOFF.md commit landed, which
is itself a good illustration of how fragile the property is).

=== F2 (INFORMATIONAL, affects how this PR gets unblocked). A DISAGREE record
    does not merely fail to count -- it FAILS the gate. ===
In the probe above, with a satisfying AGREE record present, lwb_lanes still
exited 1 and the ONLY remaining failures were:
    FAIL: reviews/32/cloud-reviewer-b.json: verdict is 'DISAGREE', want 'AGREE'
    FAIL: reviews/32/cloud-reviewer.json: verdict is 'DISAGREE', want 'AGREE'
So every DISAGREE already on a branch is a hard block, not a null vote, and a
later AGREE cannot outvote it. That applies to MY record too: filing this
DISAGREE means lwb-lanes cannot pass until the findings are addressed and the
DISAGREE records are dealt with. I record it so nobody mistakes the mechanism,
and I flag it as a design question worth an owner decision -- it is defensible
(a raised objection should not be outvoted silently) but it is not what
reviews/README.md describes, which speaks only of counting AGREEs.

=== F3 (INFORMATIONAL). My reviewed_commit and what the gate compares it to
    are NOT the same sha, by construction. ===
My brief tells me to record the full head sha I reviewed; the gate compares
reviewed_commit against resolve_reviewable_head. Here those differ: branch
head 4305428f, reviewable head 5e415c44. I reviewed the tree at 4305428f and
have recorded that sha, because inventing the other one would be recording a
commit I did not name as the one I examined. The two trees differ ONLY by
other reviewers' records under reviews/32/; no content under review differs.
Consequence, stated so it is not discovered later: the gate will read THIS
record as STALE. For a DISAGREE that costs nothing. For an AGREE it would be
silently inert -- an approval that unblocks nothing. That mismatch between the
routine's instructions and the gate's arithmetic is worth fixing before a
reviewer files an AGREE on a branch whose head is a record-only commit.

and I wrote it in while filing a finding about someone else's identity

    FAIL: reviews/32/cloud-reviewer-c.json:10: private-project name leak
I cannot read the real LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES secret, so I cannot prove the real

going red on exactly this content elsewhere, and redacting an address from a
public repository does not need proof first.

WORSE HERE THAN ON #29, AND I AM NOT SOFTENING IT: on #29 an earlier
reviewer's record already carried the same domain before I arrived. ON THIS
BRANCH MY COMMIT IS THE ONLY SOURCE. Both scans confirm it:
    working tree -> FAIL: reviews/32/cloud-reviewer-c.json:10
    range scan   -> FAIL: bbdfccfcdb81 reviews/32/cloud-reviewer-c.json:10
This commit clears the first. It CANNOT clear the second: the range scan
lwb-env-leak-history reads every line ADDED by the PR's commits and my commit
bbdfccf added that line. Force-push is denied, so I cannot repair it. I have
therefore put this branch into the same unrepairable-history state that got
#30 and #35 re-cut -- a reviewer breaking the branch it was dispatched to
unblock, which is the second time that pattern appears in my own findings on
this PR (B3 is the first, and it was someone else's commit).

The remedy is a re-cut of this branch from a commit before bbdfccf with the
content re-applied, exactly as #35 and #37 did. That is the author's call and
the owner's, not mine: I am authorized to write review records, not to
re-cut a branch.

No finding, verdict or item of evidence above is changed. Only the address is
removed, and the removal is disclosed here rather than made silently.
